sections.title: What you know
sections.content: A job ad describes a person the company does not know yet. That is the situation from the first lesson of this unit: the person may not exist, so the verb after *que* goes into the subjunctive. *Buscamos a alguien que hable inglés* means "We are looking for someone who speaks English", whoever that turns out to be.

sections.title: The language of ads
rows: Buscamos a alguien que hable inglés.
We are looking for someone who speaks English.
Se necesita una persona que tenga experiencia.
A person with experience is needed. (*Se necesita* uses the impersonal *se*; you know *se* from B1 Unit 6.)
Se busca un candidato que pueda empezar pronto.
We are looking for a candidate who can start soon.
Quiero un trabajo que pague bien.
I want a job that pays well. (A job seeker uses the same pattern.)

sections.title: Several requirements, and the person hired
sections.content: A list of requirements repeats the subjunctive and says *que* only once: *una persona que hable inglés, tenga experiencia y pueda trabajar los sábados*. When the ad is over and you talk about the person who got the job, the indicative returns, because now the person is real: *Contrataron a una candidata que habla inglés*.

items.spanish: Buscamos a alguien que sepa trabajar en equipo.
items.english: We are looking for someone who knows how to work in a team.

items.spanish: Quiero un trabajo que pague bien y tenga un buen horario.
items.english: I want a job that pays well and has good hours.

items.spanish: Contrataron a una candidata que habla inglés y tiene mucha experiencia.
items.english: They hired a candidate who speaks English and has a lot of experience.

items.spanish: Todavía no hay ningún candidato que tenga todos los requisitos.
items.english: There is still no candidate who has all the requirements.

sections.content: A list headed *Requisitos:* often uses plain infinitives (*hablar inglés, tener experiencia*), because it names the requirement in general. A sentence that describes the person you are looking for uses *que* + subjunctive.
